definitions.gloss: errand; doing business; running an errand
definitions.explanation: going out to take care of some task or business

definitions.gloss: going to the bathroom; using the toilet
definitions.explanation: a euphemistic expression for using the restroom

examples.japanese: {用足|ようた}しに{出|で}かける。
examples.english: To go out on an errand.

examples.japanese: {銀行|ぎんこう}で{用足|ようた}しをする。
examples.english: To take care of business at the bank.

examples.japanese: ちょっと{用足|ようた}しに{行|い}ってきます。
examples.english: I'll be back in a moment; I need to take care of something.

examples.japanese: {用足|ようた}しに{行|い}きたい。
examples.english: I need to use the bathroom.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{用足|ようた}しをしたがっている。
examples.english: The child needs to go to the bathroom.

examples.japanese: {外|そと}で{用足|ようた}しができない。
examples.english: I can't use the toilet outside (of home).

notes:
USAGE:
- {用足|ようた}しに{行|い}く (to go on an errand; to go to the bathroom)
- {用足|ようた}しをする (to run an errand; to use the toilet)
- {用足|ようた}しに{出|で}かける (to go out for errands)

SENSE 2 (Euphemism):
A polite, indirect way to say one needs to use the bathroom. Common with children or in formal situations.

OTHER BATHROOM EUPHEMISMS:
- お{手洗|てあら}い (bathroom - lit. hand-washing)
- トイレに{行|い}く (to go to the toilet - direct)
- {御不浄|ごふじょう} (lavatory - very formal)

RELATED WORDS:
- {用事|ようじ} (errand, business)
- {買|か}い{物|もの} (shopping)
- お{手洗|てあら}い (restroom)
